class.name: GroundSurface3D
class.brief_description: Footprints, ruts and dents in sand, soil, mud and leaf litter.
class.description: A field of dents and rims around the camera over bare ground. Nodes in [member deform_groups] press it: loaded bodies sink by Bekker's pressure-sinkage relation with Wong's soil values ([i]Theory of Ground Vehicles[/i]), the pressed material is partly compacted and partly pushed into a rim so volume is kept, and walls steeper than the material's angle of repose slump down (Sumner, O'Brien and Hodgins 1999, "Animating Sand, Mud, and Snow"). What the ground is made of follows rules per place: [member ground_type] (or [member type_map]) gives sand or soil; the moisture ([member moisture], or the [code]WeatherMap3D[/code] wetness) turns soil to mud and dry sand to damp sand, so a boot sinks 2 cm in dry sand, under 1 cm in damp sand and about 8 cm in mud, dry sand prints cave in to dishes, damp ones keep sharp walls and mud creeps back over minutes; tree crowns (the weather map's canopy closure) drop [member litter_depth] of leaf litter; bare rock from a [code]TerrainGenerator3D[/code] height source does not print, nor does ground under a [code]SnowCover3D[/code] pack. Freshly turned ground is darker until it dries ([member drying_time]); wind fills dry sand prints and rain softens them. The node draws the field as a patch with [member material], the terrain's own material, and the terrain drawn with that material (with [member BaseMaterial3D.ground_deform_enabled], or [method BaseMaterial3D.get_ground_deform_shader_code] in a shader) is lowered under the patch by [member skirt], so the prints are geometry in raster and under path tracing. Bodies keep standing on the terrain's own collider; [method get_surface_height_at] gives the printed surface for foot placement.

method.name: clear_deformation
method.description: Removes every print, including the cached tiles.

method.name: get_cached_tile_count
method.description: The number of tiles of prints kept for when the field comes back over them.

method.name: get_dent_at
method.description: How far the ground at [param position] is pressed below its undisturbed height, in metres.

method.name: get_fresh_at
method.description: How freshly turned the ground at [param position] is, from 1 (just dug) to 0 (dried).

method.name: get_ground_height_at
method.description: The undisturbed ground height at [param position], from the height source.

method.name: get_material_at
method.description: The rules at [param position]: [code]n[/code], [code]kc[/code], [code]kphi[/code] (Bekker), [code]rim_share[/code], [code]repose[/code] (degrees), [code]rate[/code] (slumping share per second), [code]max_dent[/code], [code]litter[/code] (m), [code]sand[/code] (share) and [code]deformable[/code].

method.name: get_moved_volume
method.description: The volume pressed down (x) and piled into rims (y) over the live field, in m³. Their difference is what was compacted.

method.name: get_patch_material
method.description: The copy of [member material] the patch is drawn with.

method.name: get_rim_at
method.description: How much material is piled on the ground at [param position], in metres.

method.name: get_sinkage_at
method.description: How far a body of [param mass] kg on [param area] m² ([param width] m wide, 0: from the area) sinks into the ground at [param position], in metres.

method.name: get_step_time_msec
method.description: The time the last physics step took (pressing, slumping, ageing, upload), in milliseconds.

method.name: get_surface_height_at
method.description: The printed ground height at [param position]: the undisturbed ground plus the rim minus the dent.

method.name: press
method.description: Presses the ground down to [param bottom] (world height) under a sphere of [param radius] at [param position] ([param round]) or a flat disc, plus [param sink] below the undisturbed surface. Returns the volume moved, in m³.

method.name: press_box
method.description: Presses a flat print [param size] wide (x) and long (z), turned by [param yaw] about up: a boot, a crate. Returns the volume moved, in m³.

method.name: refresh_ground
method.description: Samples the height source again (after the terrain changed).

method.name: settle
method.description: Runs slumping and ageing for [param seconds] at once, in steps of [param step].

members.member: The contact area of a [CharacterBody3D] in [member deform_groups] without a [code]ground_contact_area[/code] meta, in m² (one boot by default).
The mass of a [CharacterBody3D] in [member deform_groups] without a [code]ground_mass[/code] meta, in kg.
How close a body's underside must come to the surface to press it, in metres.
The width of the field, in metres. Prints are made only where the terrain is fully lowered: [member terrain_margin] plus [member skirt_fade] inside its edge.

Groups whose nodes press the ground. A node's first collision shape gives its footprint; rigid bodies press by their mass, characters by [member character_mass], others only to their underside. The metas [code]ground_mass[/code], [code]ground_contact_area[/code] and [code]ground_radius[/code] (or the snow ones) override.
Texels across the field (a multiple of 64).
The patch's vertex spacing over the middle half of the field, in metres.
How long freshly turned ground takes to dry to a third of its darkening, in seconds.
The node the field follows; the camera when empty.
The physics layers a downward ray finds the ground on when [member height_source] gives no height.
The spacing of the ground lattice sampled from the height source, in metres.
The ground where [member type_map] says nothing: sand or soil.

The terrain: a [code]TerrainDeformer3D[/code], a baked [code]TerrainDataMap3D[/code], a [code]TerrainGenerator3D[/code], anything with [code]get_height(position)[/code] or Terrain3D. Empty: a downward ray on [member ground_collision_mask].
The canopy closure that drops leaf litter when there is no weather map, from 0 to 1.
The leaf litter under a closed canopy, in metres; less under a thinner one.

The terrain's material. The patch is drawn with a copy of it; turn on [member BaseMaterial3D.ground_deform_enabled] on the original (or call the shader code from a [ShaderMaterial]) so the terrain is lowered under the patch. Map it by world position so the two line up.
How many tiles of prints are kept after the field leaves them.
The ground's moisture from 0 (dry) to 1 (soaked); -1 takes the [code]WeatherMap3D[/code] wetness.
The patch's vertex spacing over the outer half of the field, in metres.
How fast rain softens prints: the share lost per hour per mm/h of rain.
If [code]true[/code] and the height source is a [code]TerrainGenerator3D[/code], bare rock (exposure over one half) does not print.
How fast wind fills dry sand prints: the share lost per hour at 10 m/s, from nothing at 5 m/s (Bagnold's threshold).
How far the terrain is lowered under the patch, in metres.
Over how many metres the lowering reaches its full depth, past [member terrain_margin].
A [code]SnowCover3D[/code]: where it has more than 3 cm of snow, the snow surface takes the print instead.
How far inside the field's edge the terrain starts to be lowered, in metres; at least the terrain's vertex spacing, so no lowered triangle reaches past the patch.
A map of the ground over [member type_map_rect]: red is the share of sand, green over one half is bare rock.
The world XZ rectangle [member type_map] covers.

constants.constant: Sand: dry it caves in to dishes, damp it keeps sharp walls.
Soil: firm when dry, mud when wet.
